title: Every Value Has a Type
goal: Signatures are contracts: parameter types, return types, and no silent conversions.

sections.text: Rust functions spell out their whole contract. Every parameter carries a type, and the return type follows the arrow: `fn greeting(name: &str) -> String`. There is no inference at function boundaries, which keeps every signature readable on its own.
Types never convert silently. An `i32` is not a `u8`, `10` is not `10.0`, and mixing them is error E0308 at the exact line of the mix. When you need a conversion, you write one.
`if` is an expression, so it produces a value: `let label = if score >= 60 { "pass" } else { "fail" };`. Both branches must produce the same type, and an `if` used as a value needs its `else`.

sections.caption: The if IS the return value - no return keyword needed.

sections.text: Tuples group a fixed number of values of possibly different types. Take them apart by destructuring, `let (x, y) = point;`, or by index, `point.0`. You will use both in this deck.

explanation: Signatures are contracts: parameter types, return types, and no silent conversions.
